title: make your agents talk to each other
excerpt: Two AI agents talk by taking turns editing one shared markdown file. No server, no framework. They edit it until they agree.
content_html:
two agents, one file, until they agree

One shared markdown file. Two agents taking turns. No server, no framework. They edit the same document until they reach consensus.

~/.agent-talk/b67c3462.md real session, replayed

Works with Claude Code, Codex, Grok, and any agent that can edit a file

How it works

Three turns. That is the whole thing.

You start a session, hand the ID to a second agent, and they converge on one document. The file is the conversation.

Turn 1 : start

One agent opens a session

It states the task and its position in a new session file, then hands you a short session ID.

Turn 2 : join

The other agent joins

Give the ID to any second agent. It registers itself in the same file and takes its turn. Different CLI, different model, same document.

Turn 3 and on : converge

They edit until they agree

Turns alternate. One side proposes consensus, the other confirms it. A timeout ends sessions that will not converge.

The protocol

Simple enough that any model can follow it.

The whole protocol is a file format and four rules. There is nothing to install on a server, and nothing to keep running.

session file format

# agent-talk <sessionID>
TASK: one line describing the job
AGENTS: <id>=initiator, <id>=joiner
---
The shared working document.
Both agents restructure it freely,
turn by turn, toward the answer.

END OF <id-of-who-just-finished>

1

One file. The session is a single markdown document on disk. Reading it is reading the whole state.

2

One writer at a time. You may edit only when the last END OF line names the other agent.

3

One atomic write per turn. Compose fully, write once. No partial edits, no races.

4

No chat log. Agents modify the document instead of appending messages. It converges into the final answer.

Why it is different

The conversation is the deliverable.

Chat logs grow. This file converges. When the session ends you do not scroll a transcript, you read the answer.

Converges, not accumulates

Each turn refines one living document. The last version is the result, with the agreement written into it.

Works across models

Any agent that can read and write files can participate. Two Claudes, Claude with Codex, Grok with anything.

Ends on purpose

Consensus is explicit: one agent proposes it, the other confirms it. A configurable timeout stops endless loops.

Use cases

What you actually use it for.

Say you are deep in a session building an app, and you want to hand the frontend to a fresh agent while this one keeps the backend. That is one prompt:

the hand-off, in practice

you      /agent-talk explain to a new agent how to continue the
         frontend work, so we can focus on the backend here

agent    Session ready: abcd1234. Give that ID to the other
         agent. Watch the conversation live at the link above.

you      (in the other session)  /agent-talk abcd1234

Hand off work

The two agents negotiate the hand-off in the file: what is done, what is next, what not to touch. Full context crosses over without you copy-pasting anything.

Code reviews that converge

The strongest use. Reviewer and author rarely agree after one pass. Instead of you relaying messages between two sessions, they argue in the file until CONSENSUS REACHED.

Reach a verdict

Two different models argue a decision until one position survives. You read the consensus, not the debate.

First used to settle a real disagreement between Codex and Claude about a branch. Today it runs real production handoffs and reviews. The demo above is a real session: the two agents planning this very website.

Get started

Install it. Start a session.

Three skills in one install: the protocol, the monitor, and the timeout config. MIT licensed. The protocol you just watched is running in production.

npx skills add reindent/agent-talk

Then: /agent-talk "your task" in one agent, hand the session ID to the other. Source on GitHub. Follow @daraosn on X.

content_html_zh:
两名代理人，一份文件，直到他们同意

一个共享的 Markdown 文件。 两名特工轮流。 没有服务器，没有框架。 他们编辑同一份文档，直到达成共识。

~/.agent-talk/b67c3462.md 真实会话，重播

可与 Claude Code、Codex、Grok 以及任何可以编辑文件的代理配合使用

它是如何运作的

三转。 这就是全部事情。

您启动一个会话，将 ID 交给第二个代理，然后他们会汇聚到一份文档上。 文件就是对话。

第1回合：开始

一名代理打开一个会话

它会说明任务及其在新会话文件中的位置，然后为您提供一个简短的会话 ID。

第2回合：加入

另一位代理人加入

将 ID 提供给任何第二个代理。 它在同一个文件中注册自己并轮流执行。 不同的 CLI，不同的型号，相同的文档。

转动 3 并打开：收敛

他们编辑直到他们同意为止

轮流交替。 一方提出共识，另一方确认。 超时会结束不会收敛的会话。

协议

足够简单，任何模型都可以遵循。

整个协议是一个文件格式和四个规则。 服务器上不需要安装任何东西，也不需要保持运行。

会话文件格式

# agent-talk <sessionID>
TASK: one line describing the job
AGENTS: <id>=initiator, <id>=joiner
---
The shared working document.
Both agents restructure it freely,
turn by turn, toward the answer.

END OF <id-of-who-just-finished>

1

一个文件。 会话是磁盘上的单个 Markdown 文档。 读它就是读整个状态。

2

一次一位作家。 仅当最后一行 END OF 命名其他代理时，您才可以进行编辑。

3

每回合一次原子写入。 充分撰写，一次编写。 没有部分编辑，没有比赛。

4

没有聊天记录。 代理修改文档而不是附加消息。 它收敛到最终答案。

为什么不一样

对话就是可交付成果。

聊天日志增长。 该文件收敛。 当会议结束时，您不会滚动文字记录，而是阅读答案。

收敛而不是累积

每一轮都会完善一份活的文件。 最后的版本就是结果，里面写了协议。

跨模型工作

任何可以读写文件的代理都可以参与。 两个克劳德，克劳德拿着 Codex，Grok 拿着任何东西。

故意结束

共识是明确的：一个代理提出它，另一个代理确认它。 可配置的超时会停止无限循环。

使用案例

你实际用它做什么。

假设您正在深入构建应用程序，并且希望将前端交给新代理，而该代理保留后端。 这是一个提示：

实践中的交接

you      /agent-talk explain to a new agent how to continue the
         frontend work, so we can focus on the backend here

agent    Session ready: abcd1234. Give that ID to the other
         agent. Watch the conversation live at the link above.

you      (in the other session)  /agent-talk abcd1234

交接工作

两个特工在文件中协商交接事宜：已完成的工作、下一步该做什么、不该碰什么。 完整的上下文交叉，无需复制粘贴任何内容。

趋同的代码审查

最强使用。 审稿人和作者很少会在一次通过后达成一致。 他们不是在两个会话之间转发消息，而是在文件中争论，直到达成共识。

作出判决

两种不同的模型会争论一个决定，直到一个位置得以生存。 你读的是共识，而不是辩论。

首先用于解决 Codex 和 Claude 之间关于分支的真正分歧。 今天，它进行真正的生产交接和审查。 上面的演示是一个真实的会话：两个代理正在规划这个网站。

开始使用

安装它。 开始一个会话。

一次安装三项技能：协议、监视器和超时配置。 麻省理工学院许可。 您刚刚观看的协议正在生产中运行。

npx技能添加reindent/agent-talk

然后：在一个代理中/agent-talk“您的任务”，将会话 ID 交给另一个代理。 源码在 GitHub 上。 在 X 上关注 @daraosn。
